messages:
harper: Hi team, quick Q about orthodontics pre-auth + FSA. My kid's ortho gave a treatment plan starting 2026-04-01 with total cost $4,200 and a monthly payment schedule. Our plan mentions orthodontia for dependents covered at 50% after deductible but requires pre-authorization. Do I need to submit the entire treatment plan up front to get pre-auth? Also, can I use my FSA for the patient portion as they bill monthly?

benefits-bot: Quick link: coverage details at https://benefits.redwood.com/plans > Dental. Pre-auth required for orthodontics > $500. FSA eligible for orthodontic expenses; check IRS rules for plan year.

Lena: Hey Harper  congrats on the plan being ready. Two parts: 1) Pre-auth: yes, carrier typically needs the full treatment plan + itemized estimate (CPT codes, duration, start date) to issue pre-authorization and estimate of payable amount. Submit via portal Claims > Pre-auths or email dental@redwood.com and we'll attach to carrier case. 2) FSA: you can use FSA for patient-responsible portion. Options: submit a Letter of Medical Necessity (LMN) if needed for recurring payments, or submit receipts monthly for reimbursement. Some providers can accept FSA debit card for monthly installments if they provide itemized statements.

harper: Thanks. The ortho provided a 24-month plan with monthly billing and a one-time banding fee. They listed codes 4340/4361 in the estimate. I'll upload the treatment plan. A couple more clarifications: will pre-auth lock in the carrier estimate for the whole course, or can allowed amounts change year-to-year? Also, I want to use leftover FSA funds from 2026 plan year; do I need receipts dated in 2026 to claim?

Lena: Good Qs. Usually pre-auth gives an estimate based on current fee schedule and plan terms; insurer may re-evaluate if treatment spans plan years or if plan changes (rare mid-year). If treatment crosses plan years, allowed amounts can change at renewal. For FSA: reimbursement requires expense incurred during the FSA coverage period. If your FSA plan year is calendar year, services dated in 2026 are eligible for 2026 funds. If you have a grace period or carryover, check your FSA plan doc. We can confirm your plan year details if you tell me your enrollment tier and plan code.

harper: I'm on Redwood Plus Dental (DP-PLUS-2026). Uploading treatment plan now. Also, ortho said they could bill insurance directly and then bill me for patient portion monthly. If insurer pays allowed amount up front to provider, can we submit the patient portion to FSA as recurring expense?

flex-admin: Hi Harper  for FSA reimbursements: you can submit patient portion receipts as they are billed/paid. If provider applies insurance payments first and then invoices you monthly, each invoice with proof of payment is eligible. For recurring installments, many employees submit monthly statements + proof of payment. Alternatively, you can submit an LMN to cover the full course and request an advance reimbursement if your FSA plan allows it; we'll need provider signature and diagnosis code. Check your FSA plan's advance rules in your summary plan description.

harper: Great, thanks. Please open the pre-auth with carrier and mark that treatment starts 2026-04-01. I authorize benefits team to share the treatment plan. Also, any suggestions to avoid surprise denials later?

Lena: Action: I'll open a pre-auth case with the carrier once the plan is uploaded. Tips to reduce denials: ensure ortho includes diagnosis code, CPT codes, banding/start date, and indicates dependent relationship. Confirm dependent is listed on digital ID with correct DOB. Upload any prior service history if they did previous work. We'll request a written pre-auth estimate from carrier (we'll attach to your portal).

harper: Uploaded plan and consent form. Member ID 881233445. Dependent DOB 2014-09-02.

Lena: Received. Case submitted to carrier as PREAUTH-20260325-88. Expected carrier response 7-10 business days. We'll post the pre-auth ID and the estimated payable amount when it comes back. If carrier denies or reduces coverage, we'll work with broker and the provider to appeal. :thumbsup:
